summary: Steel lookout near Aristes, Columbia County: register says built 1919 and removed 1975; notices show 1920s rebuilds, staffing into the 1940s, and a 1976 removal sale.

facts.design: Steel tower; register calls it a steel Aermotor tower; newspaper notices describe an 80-foot steel tower from 1927-28
facts.status_note: Register says removed in 1975, but a May 1976 state notice still offered the tower for sale for removal
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters

events.note: Register date: built by the AFPA; 1920-21 notices do not match it cleanly
Directors of the Anthracite Forest Protective Association ordered reconstruction; a 64-foot steel observation tower was planned
Notice says a tower had been erected in the vicinity of Aristes, ordered after a serious fire the year before
Tower dynamited; property stolen from it recovered in Centralia; state said it would prosecute
Watchman in the tower had to call Mount Carmel for fire fighters until a local fire company was formed at Aristes
State inspectors condemned the structure over weak concrete piers and unstable ladders; towerman Mat Smith put on patrol duty
Plan for an 80-foot steel tower at a new site near Aristes to replace an older tower several miles east that was unsafe
March 1928 notice says the Aristes tower was reconstructed that year
Sylvester Beaver went on duty at the Aristes tower
A fire was discovered south of Centralia soon after telephone connections were placed
Beaver had manned the Aristes tower for 18 consecutive years and had reported many forest fires
Register gives 1975 as the removal year; disputed by a May 1976 notice
State notice offers the Aristes Fire Tower for sale to the highest bidder for removal

corrections.why: Newspaper notices describe the Aristes tower as 80 feet tall from 1927 to 1938 (24.4 m); no page read supports 3.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says built 1919. 1920 notices describe an order to reconstruct the Aristes fire tower and a planned 64-foot steel tower, and an April 1921 notice says a tower had been erected. The story gives the register date as its claim and says the date is unsettled.
Register gives 1975 as the removal year. A May 1976 state notice still offered the tower for sale for removal, so the sources do not agree on when it came down.

Register credits the AFPA. The 1920 notice names the Anthracite Forest Protective Association, and a 1922 notice names the Pennsylvania Fire Protective Association. The story does not settle which name is right.

notes_for_editor: Build and removal dates conflict: register says 1919 and 1975; notices suggest a tower in 1920-21 and a removal sale in May 1976. Brief height 3.7 m is unsupported; notices say 64 ft planned (1920) and 80 ft (1927-1938), so 24.4 m is proposed. All newspaper material comes through one transcription page; the original papers were not read. No source describes the site today; the Mapcarta point labelled Centralia Fire Tower may or may not be this lookout. Access is not stated in any source.
